story.title: Bryan Kohberger Seeks to Withdraw Guilty Plea in Idaho Student Murders
story.summary: Bryan Kohberger, who pleaded guilty to the murders of four University of Idaho students in 2022, is now seeking to withdraw his guilty plea. This request follows his admission as part of a plea deal, and he is aiming to go to trial instead. Kohberger has filed a petition for post-conviction relief regarding his conviction.

explore_lenses.label: Why does reopening the plea matter?
explore_lenses.title: It would challenge the case’s final resolution
explore_lenses.summary: Kohberger’s plea agreement ended the capital prosecution with four consecutive life-without-parole sentences. A successful post-conviction challenge could undo that judgment and restore the prospect of litigation over the charges.

claims.text: The July 2025 plea agreement required guilty pleas to four first-degree murder counts and burglary; it specified four fixed consecutive life sentences and a fixed 10-year burglary sentence.
The agreement records that Kohberger waived a jury trial, confrontation rights, self-incrimination protections, defenses, appeal rights, and a Rule 35 sentence-reduction motion.
The Goncalves family said Kohberger received the deal he sought, which spared his life, and disputed the idea that he had previously indicated he was pressured or uninformed.

explore_lenses.uncertainty_note: The filing itself does not vacate the convictions or sentences; the court has not yet ruled on the requested relief.

explore_lenses.label: What is Kohberger claiming was wrong?
explore_lenses.title: He alleges coercion and inadequate legal advice
explore_lenses.summary: Kohberger’s petition alleges that his plea was not knowing or voluntary because of his lawyers’ conduct and allegedly undisclosed evidence. Those are allegations in a self-represented filing, and they conflict with his prior sworn plea statements and the signed agreement.

claims.text: Kohberger alleges his attorneys induced a false confession through coercion, threats, false promises and disinformation, including claims that potentially helpful evidence was not disclosed or reviewed during plea negotiations.
He specifically cited an “unknown hair in Chapin’s hand” and alleged that counsel misrepresented the conditions of life imprisonment and death row.
The signed plea agreement says he was not coerced, was satisfied with counsel, had reviewed possible defenses, and voluntarily waived those defenses and constitutional claims.
At the July 2025 plea hearing, Kohberger answered yes when asked whether he was pleading guilty because he was guilty, according to contemporaneous reporting on the proceeding.

explore_lenses.label: What must happen before any new trial?
explore_lenses.title: He must clear a high post-conviction bar
explore_lenses.summary: Because Kohberger has already been sentenced, the request proceeds through a separate post-conviction civil case rather than an ordinary appeal. He bears the burden to prove a ground for relief, and withdrawal after sentencing requires correction of a “manifest injustice.”

claims.text: Idaho Criminal Rule 39 requires post-conviction relief to be sought by petition in the convicting district court as a separate civil case, and places the burden on the petitioner to prove grounds for relief by a preponderance of the evidence.
Idaho Criminal Rule 33(c) permits withdrawal of a guilty plea after judgment only to correct a “manifest injustice.”

University of Idaho law professor Samuel Newton said Kohberger would need concrete, credible evidence that material misinformation or ineffective assistance made his plea involuntary or unknowing, and would need to explain his earlier sworn statements.
Forecast: Newton characterized the chances of success as “slim to none,” citing the extensive on-the-record plea process; that is an expert assessment, not a court ruling.

related_stories.summary: A shooting at a food festival in Seattle resulted in the deaths of three individuals, with four others injured, including a two-year-old boy. Authorities have indicated that the incident may be gang-related. One suspect is in custody, while another remains at large as investigations continue.

related_stories.title: Ariana Grande Sues Hackers for Stolen Unreleased Music and Content
related_stories.summary: Ariana Grande has filed a lawsuit against unidentified hackers who allegedly stole her unreleased music, photos, and videos. In her complaint, she claims that the breach has caused 'irreparable harm' to her career and is seeking a court order to compel internet providers to reveal the hackers' identities.

related_stories.title: Trial Set for Singer D4vd in Murder of 14-Year-Old Celeste Rivas Hernandez
related_stories.summary: Singer D4vd, whose real name is David Anthony Burke, has been ordered to stand trial for the murder of 14-year-old Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Prosecutors allege that he dismembered her body, which was found in a Tesla registered to him. The trial follows a judge's ruling that sufficient evidence exists to proceed with the case.

related_stories.title: Gunfire Targets US Consulate in Toronto Again This Year
related_stories.summary: Shots were fired at the US consulate in Toronto, marking the second incident of this nature this year. Police engaged in a high-speed chase but did not apprehend the suspect, who remains at large. This follows a similar attack in June, which resulted in the arrest of three individuals.
